findings.evidence: AEMO 2026 gives November 2031 as proponent timing for the whole VIC-NSW interconnector (Stage 2), not for the NSW component. The South West NSW REZ component's proponent timing is August 2029 (AEMO's earlier assumption was June 2030). A separate, earlier milestone is now archived: Transgrid's project page states the EIS for the NSW section was placed on public exhibition in August 2025, and NSW DPHI is reviewing the EIS, Amendment Report and Submissions Report toward a final approval decision by the State and Commonwealth governments anticipated in late 2026 (VNN-AO-2025-TG-EIS-EXHIBITED; VNN-AO-2026-TG-APPROVAL-TIMING). This is an approval-decision milestone, not a completion or in-service date, and does not change the 2029/2031 timing evidence.
findings.pages: HUM-AEMO-2026-ISP-A5 pp52-53; VNN-TG-2026-PROJECTPAGE captured HTML page

findings.evidence: No archived source states a NSW-only whole-project cost. The chart's 3.7 is half of a whole-interconnector amount, matched by the identical 3.7 in the VNI West (VIC) row. The only current whole-VNI figure is $7,600m ($2025, Class 4, two Dinawan transformers) per VNN-AO-2026-VNIWEST-TOTAL, which halves to 3.8, not 3.7; historical whole-VNI figures are VNN-AO-2024-VNIWEST-3499, VNN-AO-2024-VNIWEST-3614 and, from the AER, $3,963.6m ($Real 2022-23, VNN-AO-2024-AER-VNIWEST-TOTAL). The exact input the author halved is not reconstructible from the archive. The only NSW-specific approved amount now archived is the AER's stage 1 early works determination: Transgrid proposed $1,096.3 million ($Real 2022-23) for the New South Wales portion of the project (VNN-AO-2024-AER-CPA-PROPOSED), and the AER substituted $948.8 million ($Real 2022-23, VNN-AO-2024-AER-CPA-APPROVED). Both are a partial, stage 1 early works boundary, not the whole NSW component cost the chart cell implies, so neither resolves the chart's 3.7.
findings.pages: HUM-AEMO-2026-ISP-A5 p52; HUM-AEMO-2024-ISP-A5 p45; VNN-AER-2024-CPADETERMINATION pp3, 6-7

findings.evidence: AEMO 2026 states a +1,800 MW expansion of REZ transfer capacity from Dinawan, but only as the separately modelled N5 Option 2 third-transformer increment above the base N5 figure of 600 MW; it is not the NSW component's base capacity. AEMO 2020 separately reported +1,800 MW southward VIC-NSW transfer for the Kerang route, a different (whole-interconnector, superseded) boundary.

PACR Table 6 (p48) gives an approximate NSW line length of 203 km for preferred Option 5A (184 km was Option 5, superseded). This is an indicative corridor-stage length between Dinawan and the WRL connection, not a built 500 kV trunk length as the chart defines it; no NSW-specific length is stated elsewhere.

Workbook ratio of the chart's own cost and trunk cells (3.7 billion / 240 km). The cost cell is an author split with no NSW-only whole-project figure archived (see cost_aud_billion), and the trunk cell's only archived figure (184 km, a PACR cost-estimating assumption, not the chart's boundary) does not match the chart's 240 km, so the ratio cannot be validated against any archived source.

AEMO 2026 describes upgrading the existing Dinawan - Wagga Wagga - Gugaa double-circuit line from 330 kV to 500 kV operation with a bypass at Wagga Wagga. Two circuits are therefore uprated existing circuits (built at 500 kV under Project EnergyConnect and HumeLink), not new-build circuits.

The NSW component's line scope is the single Dinawan - Wagga Wagga - Gugaa double-circuit corridor, plus a Gugaa cut-in and a rebuild of a section of line TL51 between Gugaa and Wagga on the existing easement, which the source does not count as lines.

Alternative-route counting is an author definition no source supplies. AEMO 2020 did present Shepparton and Kerang route alternatives for VNI West, and the current route was selected as option 5A in the May 2023 RIT-T, so a zero depends entirely on the author's definition of a live alternative.

No archived source states a synchronous condenser rating for the South West NSW REZ component. The 2026 scope list names 500 kV line shunt reactors and reactor reconfiguration but no synchronous condensers, which is not a stated zero.

No source calls any NSW element a hub. The Dinawan 500 kV switchyard is a switchyard with 500/330 kV transformers and line reactors; the source does not describe it as a REZ hosting hub, so counting it as one hub is an author definition.

AEMO 2026 specifies three 500/330 kV 1,500 MVA transformers at the Dinawan switchyard in the N5 Option 1 / Option 2 Stage 1 scope, and states that the $7,600m cost includes two transformers only. Neither the two-transformer nor the three-transformer configuration reaches 6,000 MVA at the stated 1,500 MVA unit rating; the 2024 scope named two such transformers.
No archived source states a feeder-line length for the South West NSW REZ component, and the sources do not use a feeder-line category, so the zero is neither supported nor contradicted.

policy_chart.overall_status: The row describes a NSW half of a project whose archived cost, capacity and timing evidence exists only at whole-interconnector or conditional-option boundaries, so its headline cost is an author split, its transformer rating is contradicted, and its route, syncon and feeder cells are unsupported.

summary.analysis_conclusion: Every archived monetary figure is a whole-VNI West boundary ($7,600m 2026; $3,499m 2024 inclusive of WRL; $3,614m modelled). No archived source allocates a NSW share, so the chart's 3.7 is an author split of a whole-interconnector amount, not a sourced NSW cost.
summary.capacity: AEMO 2026 reports REZ N5: 600 MW, plus a separately modelled +1,800 MW REZ transfer from Dinawan conditional on a third Dinawan transformer (N5 Option 2). The interconnector Stage 2 adds forward 1,890 MW / reverse 1,670 MW.
summary.completion_date: South West NSW REZ component: August 2029 (proponent advice, 2026 ISP). Whole VIC-NSW link: November 2031.
summary.current_status: Actionable NSW project progressing under the Electricity Infrastructure Investment Act 2020 (NSW); RIT-T concluded May 2023 (option 5A) and feedback loop confirmed December 2023; early works under way.
summary.delivery_status: Early works, community engagement and technical studies; Iberdrola awarded the design-and-develop contract in November 2025 (Victorian side, with TCV). No NSW construction outturn captured.
summary.dependent_projects: HumeLink and Project EnergyConnect are stated prerequisites for the South West NSW REZ Stage 1 scope; Western Renewables Link is a prerequisite for Stage 2 and its cost was bundled into the 2024 $3,499m figure.
summary.funding_pathway: NSW Electricity Infrastructure Investment Act 2020 pathway for the South West NSW REZ component; NSW Government announced $225m in the 2026 NSW Budget (funding announcement, not project cost, allowance or outturn).
summary.identity: AEMO treats VNI West as one integrated 500 kV interconnector from near Bulgana (Vic) to Dinawan (NSW); the South West NSW REZ component is separately categorised as an actionable NSW project. This pack curates the NSW component; no NSW-only cost, route or capacity is excised from the whole-project figures.

summary.owner: Transgrid (NSW) with VicGrid/TCV in Victoria; Transgrid and AVP (now VicGrid) were the RIT-T proponents. Transgrid's own scope/approval records were unavailable.
summary.schedule: Proponent timing for the South West NSW REZ component is August 2029 (earlier AEMO assumption June 2030); VIC-NSW Stage 2 proponent timing is November 2031.
summary.trunk_voltage_kv: 500 kV (interconnector); NSW component upgrades the Dinawan - Wagga Wagga - Gugaa double-circuit line from 330 kV to 500 kV operation.

warnings.finding: The chart's 3.7 cost is half of a whole-interconnector amount: the VNI West (NSW) and VNI West (VIC) rows carry the identical 3.7, and no archived source states a NSW-only cost. The only current whole-VNI figure, $7,600m ($2025, Class 4, two transformers), halves to 3.8, so the halved input cannot be identified in the archive.
warnings.implication: The cell must not be published as a NSW project cost. Either restate it as an explicitly labelled half of the $7,600m whole-project amount or leave it unsourced.

warnings.finding: Splitting the bundled $7,600m 'South West NSW REZ + Interconnector' amount into NSW and Victorian halves is an author decision with no source basis.
warnings.implication: The author must decide whether to publish a split at all, and on what stated rule; the pack records no NSW allocation.

warnings.finding: Attribution of the Dinawan works (500 kV switchyard, the two or three 500/330 kV transformers, and the Dinawan-end reactors brought forward from the Dinawan - Tragowel circuits) between the NSW component and the interconnector is not resolved by any archived source.
warnings.implication: The author must decide which Dinawan elements count as NSW component scope before any NSW-level count or cost is published.

warnings.finding: The NSW/Victoria lifecycle relationship is dual: AEMO states VNI West remains one actionable integrated ISP project and that integrated delivery is more efficient than staging, while categorising the South West NSW REZ component as an actionable NSW project under the Electricity Infrastructure Investment Act 2020 (NSW).
warnings.implication: The author must decide whether the chart treats VNI West (NSW) as a project in its own right or as a component of one project, since the two readings imply different rows.

warnings.finding: The hubs cell (1) rests on an author definition: no source describes the Dinawan 500 kV switchyard, or any other NSW element, as a hosting hub.
warnings.implication: Publish the hub count only with a stated author definition, or leave the cell blank.

warnings.finding: The alt_routes cell (0) rests on an author definition. AEMO 2020 assessed Shepparton and Kerang route alternatives and the current alignment was selected as option 5A in May 2023.
warnings.implication: The author must state whether historical or superseded alternatives count before publishing a zero.

warnings.finding: The chart states 6,000 MVA of transformers. AEMO 2026 specifies three 500/330 kV 1,500 MVA units at Dinawan and says the $7,600m includes two transformers only; AEMO 2024 specified two such units.
warnings.implication: No archived configuration reaches 6,000 MVA at the stated unit rating; the cell should be corrected or its basis stated.

warnings.finding: The $116m third-transformer increment is modelled separately above the $7,600m amount, which includes two transformers only; the $7,600m itself bundles the South West NSW REZ with the interconnector and contains $565m of approved early works and other incurred costs excluded from the ISP CBA.
warnings.implication: Do not form $7,716m, do not net out the $565m, and do not treat any portion as a NSW allocation.

warnings.finding: The 2020 cost ranges, the 2024 $3,499m (2020-21 dollars, inclusive of WRL) and $3,614m (real 2023 dollars, WRL removed), and the 2026 $7,600m ($2025, Class 4) differ in route, scope, dollar year and maturity.
warnings.implication: Do not build a revision series or compute growth between them; each is a discrete dated observation.
warnings.pinpoints: HUM-AEMO-2020-ISP-A3 pp33-36; HUM-AEMO-2024-ISP-A5 p45; HUM-AEMO-2026-ISP-A5 p52

warnings.finding: The 2024 $3,499m is stated to be inclusive of the $315m Western Renewables Link project, and the option included relocating and uprating the WRL terminal station and line; the 2026 $7,600m has a different bundle (South West NSW REZ + Interconnector) with WRL a prerequisite.
warnings.implication: Cross-family double counting is possible against the Western Renewables Link row; boundaries must be stated wherever these figures appear.

warnings.finding: The Dinawan - Wagga Wagga - Gugaa circuits being upgraded were built at 500 kV under Project EnergyConnect and HumeLink, both stated prerequisites of the NSW component.
warnings.implication: Circuit, line and km counts attributed to VNI West (NSW) overlap physical assets delivered and costed by other project families.

warnings.finding: The $116m third-transformer increment is published without a stated price basis, and the $225m NSW funding announcement states no price basis or publication date.
warnings.implication: Neither amount may be escalated, deflated or compared with the $2025 $7,600m figure.
warnings.pinpoints: HUM-AEMO-2026-ISP-A5 p52 footnote 103; ATE15-EC-FUND-1 derivative line 278

warnings.finding: The EnergyCo NSW VNI West project page returned HTTP 404 on both attempted official routes on 2026-09-03.
warnings.implication: The NSW delivery-body account of scope and status is unavailable; only the funding announcement page was captured.

warnings.finding: NSW statutory planning records (NSW Planning Portal major-projects page for VNI West) returned HTTP 404 on both attempted routes on 2026-09-03.
warnings.implication: No NSW planning approval, authorisation or determination may be asserted for the NSW component.

warnings.finding: A regulatory determination and its underlying contingent project application are now captured for the NSW component: the AER's May 2024 determination on Transgrid's VNI West Stage 1 early works CPA ($948.8m approved of $1,096.3m proposed). No construction outturn was captured, and the November 2025 Iberdrola contract award is known only through AEMO's narrative.
warnings.implication: The AER determination is a regulatory allowance for stage 1 early works, not a construction outturn; all monetary values in this pack, including the AER amounts, remain proponent estimates or regulatory allowances, not outturn costs.

warnings.finding: The joint VNI West PADR and PACR are now archived as primary sources (VNV-TRANSGRID-2022-PADR; VNV-TRANSGRID-2023-PACR, shared under sources/vni-west-victoria/manifest.csv), so the RIT-T cost and NSW-length evidence in this pack is no longer secondhand through AEMO alone. The EnergyCo funding page still carries no asserted publication date or funding terms, and the EnergyCo and NSW Planning Portal VNI West project pages remain unavailable (see SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE warnings).
warnings.implication: Re-check when NSW funding terms are published and when the EnergyCo VNI West project page or NSW Planning Portal record become available.
